review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: There is an opinion that the news media have too much impact on people's daily lives and this is a negative development. I believe that despite being so influential, the news media don't just have negative effects.

It is true that the widespread access to smartphones and Internet services has enable people to stay up to date with the news instantly regardless of wherever and whenever they are. Eventually, the news will become a regular part of their daily routine which is hard to completely ignore. Moreover, the intense competition among news outlets also contribute to this problem. In order to gain attention from people, most media agencies focus on shocking and breaking content and present it in a highly sensationalised manner combining with dramatic headlines and eye-catching visuals leading to the overall impact of news on public opinion being reinforced.

However, I strongly believe that it is not just a negative development. Admittedly, exposure to a constant stream of distressing and exaggerated news can overwhelm people leading to them having overly anxious and helpless feelings even in situations that do not directly affect them. However, the news coverage helps warn the public to existing and looming problems in society such as crime, natural disasters, or political corruption so that individuals are better informed and more prepared to respond to potential threats, which is positively contributing to handling risks in an increasingly complex society.
In conclusion, although it is true that news media influence may cause a certain issue, those potential dangers pale in comparison with the benefit it brings.

completion.comment: Em đã viết đủ bốn phần trên hai trang nguồn đã xác minh.

review.overall: Em triển khai đủ bốn nhánh, có thêm ý riêng rằng thói quen đọc tin khó bỏ, và giữ được hướng tin tức không chỉ gây hại. Cần bổ sung câu chủ đề bao quát Body 1, sửa has enable và competition contribute, đồng thời bỏ viết tắt. Câu kết hiện khẳng định lợi ích vượt xa tác hại dù thân bài mới nêu hai mặt; em cần chốt đúng mức đã chứng minh. Cô giữ toàn bộ các chuỗi ý và cách diễn đạt đúng của em.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: There is an opinion that students who performs best in academic fields should be rewarded, while others think it is more important to praise students who show improvements. Personally, I think both groups deserve their own reward for their effort.

Admittedly, students with outstanding academic results obviously have diligently applied themselves to their studies, so obviously they deserve their praises and privileges which will give them advantages and opportunity in the future. Because of those rewards, these students and others are encouraged to study harder in order to win these. them, leading to propelling towards overall academic gains. This kind of competition is seen in almost every aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded. Being in a competitive environment at early can make students be accustomed to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, enabling them to achieve success more easily in later life.

However, students who are improving also needs encouraging from schools. In a highly competitive environment, only a few smart students can reach the top and receive the rewards. If others are not rewarded, it may cause them to think that their effort is futile because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals. This may cause them to gradually lose the incentive to study. Moreover, emphasizing improvements may encourage all students to be diligent in studies, helping them to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. And that the constant desire to outdo themselves even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against others.
In conclusion, I believe that students who show their hard-working and improvements constantly always deserve praises regardless of their academic performance.

review.overall: Em viết đủ bốn phần và mở bài chọn thưởng cả hai nhóm. Body 1 nối công sức với sự ghi nhận rồi chuyển sang môi trường cạnh tranh; Body 2 nêu được cảm giác nỗ lực vô ích và động lực tự vượt mình. Tuy vậy, câu kết chỉ gọi nhóm chăm chỉ/tiến bộ, chưa chốt rõ nhóm đạt kết quả cao như lập trường ban đầu. Việc ghép 'them, leading to propelling' và 'Being in a competitive environment at early' còn làm đứt mạch Body 1; 'students ... needs' sai hòa hợp. Em cần viết lại các câu bị ghép, nêu đủ hai nhóm ở kết luận và tự soát chủ ngữ–động từ. Body 1 có đủ công sức và cạnh tranh, nhưng câu mở đã chứa lý do công sức; câu về cạnh tranh được nhận ra nhờ đổi nội dung, còn thiếu mốc bổ sung ở bài gốc. Body 2 có “Moreover” cho ý thứ hai nhưng ý đầu chưa được giới thiệu rõ sau câu chủ đề.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that students who perform best in academic fields should be rewarded, while others think it is more important to praise students who show improvements. Personally, I think both groups deserve rewards for their efforts.

Admittedly, students with outstanding academic results should be rewarded. The primary reason is that they have diligently applied themselves to their studies. Therefore, they deserve their praises and privileges which will give them advantages and opportunities in the future. These rewards may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, thereby contributing to overall academic gains. Moreover, this kind of competition is seen in almost every aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded. Being in a competitive environment from an early age can help students become accustomed to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, enabling them to achieve success more easily in later life.

However, students who are improving also need encouragement from schools. The first concern is that in a highly competitive environment, only a few smart students can reach the top and receive the rewards. If others are not rewarded, it may cause them to think that their effort is futile. This is because they feel unable to surpass those outstanding individuals. This may cause them to gradually lose the incentive to study. Moreover, emphasizing improvements may encourage all students to be diligent in studies, helping them to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. This constant desire to outdo themselves may even benefit them more than the determination to win against others.
In conclusion, I believe that both students with the best academic results and those who consistently work hard and improve deserve praise.

Some people think that school should reward students who show the best academic results, while others believe that it is more important to reward students who show improvements.
Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: In some countries, parents refuse to send their children, instead, they decide to teach children themselves believing that it brings more benefits than traditional education. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought.

Firstly, people who support home schooling often argue that it allows parents to save money since no school fees are required. Plus, home-educated children are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure which both can lead to health and mental problems. In addition, parents who teach their children at home can tailor their own curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young children which is often not the case in traditional school because of large class size.

However, these so-called advantages turn out to be harmful to children's development. This educational approach does not actually save money because parents need to pay a large amount of money for teach equipment and tutors, also, one parents needs to be cut off to cater for their child's needs, be these academic or personal. Another problem is that most parents might not be well-versed in all school subjects leading to difficulties in properly explaining concepts for children and ultimately results in academic problems. Finally, even the problems that children are faced with at school like bullying and having romantic feelings for others can prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.
In conclusion, given the disadvantages of home schooling, it can not replace the traditional school and can only be applied in some special situations.
review.overall: Em có bốn đoạn và giữ quan điểm trường học có lợi hơn. Body 1 nêu đủ ba lợi ích; Body 2 có tiền bạc, chuyên môn và tình huống xã hội. Tuy nhiên, mở bài 'parents refuse to send' đẩy sắc thái từ lựa chọn sang từ chối; 'health and mental problems' không đúng với ý ảnh hưởng cảm xúc/tâm lý. Câu 'most parents might not be well-versed ... leading ... and ultimately results' lẫn hai dạng động từ, còn kết bài chuyển sang 'chỉ áp dụng trong vài hoàn cảnh' mà Body chưa giải thích. Em cần giữ câu hỏi cân lợi–hại và tự soát quan hệ nghĩa, cấu trúc câu.

paragraphs: In some countries, parents choose to teach their children at home instead of sending them to school as they believe it brings more benefits than traditional education. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought: the disadvantages are greater.

People who support homeschooling often argue that it brings several benefits. Firstly, it allows parents to save money since no school fees are required. Plus, home-educated children are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, both of which can lead to emotional and mental problems. In addition, parents who teach their children at home can tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young children, which is often not the case in traditional schools owing to large classes.

However, these apparent advantages come with substantial drawbacks. Initially, this approach may not actually save money as parents need to pay for teaching equipment and tutors. One parent may also need to set aside working time to cater for the child's academic or personal needs. Another problem is that most parents might not be well versed in all school subjects, which can make it difficult to explain concepts properly and may lead to academic problems. Finally, even problems that children face at school, such as bullying and having romantic feelings for others, can prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.
In conclusion, given these disadvantages, I believe homeschooling's drawbacks outweigh its benefits, and traditional schooling remains the better choice.
